rounds.text: Creative Newtech Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line compounding, with compounded sales growth over 5 years hitting 39% [E14] and compounded profit growth over 5 years reaching 45% [E17]. This robust operational performance is matched by superior capital efficiency, evidenced by a 5-year median return on equity of 21% [E23] and a robust ROCE of 18.8% [E12], both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks like the sector median ROCE of 7.1% [E67]. Valuation metrics indicate potential under-appreciation, as a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at Rs 2021 per share against a market price of Rs 1033 [E41], leaving a substantial margin of safety of 48.9% [E42]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF suggests the current market price only prices in 8.8% earnings growth, which is markedly below the base case assumption of 18.0% [E43]. Institutional confidence is visibly building, marked by positive money flow and a holding increase of 1.16 percentage points [E40], alongside a rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 signaling a high-confidence buy [E58]. Conceded: [E30], [E31], [E32], [E57].

Creative Newtech Ltd exhibits severe cash generation and liquidity risks that completely undermine its reported earnings growth. Operating cash flow turned aggressively negative to Rs -272 Cr in Mar 2026, driving free cash flow down to Rs -275 Cr [E31, E32]. This collapse yields a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -3.89x against reported profit, indicating that earnings are entirely detached from actual cash collections [E30]. Compounding this liquidity drain, borrowings spiked dramatically to Rs 324 Cr in Mar 2026, up sharply from Rs 72 Cr just a year prior [E35]. Furthermore, deteriorating working capital efficiency is evidenced by debtor days stretching from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E57]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 20.9x with strong historical sales and profit growth CAGRs [E1, E14, E17]. However, the stock commands a premium valuation with EV/EBITDA of 16.87x and P/B of 4.23x against sector benchmarks while exhibiting high annualised volatility of 52.8% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% [E6, E7, E11, E49, E50].

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -272 Cr and free cash flow was Rs -275 Cr in Mar 2026, leading to a negative cash conversion ratio of -3.89x and a surge in borrowings to Rs 324 Cr [E30, E31, E32, E35]. Conceded: debtor days expanded to 76.3 and historical volatility sits at 52.8% with a past drawdown of -51.3% [E49, E50, E57]. However, this severe liquidity snapshot must be weighed against robust structural profitability, featuring a 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth of 45% and 36% respectively, alongside a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 36% [E17, E18, E19]. The core operational strength is further validated by a superior return on capital employed of 14.89% against a sector benchmark of 6.91%, and a return on equity of 19.33% that vastly outperforms the sector's 5.35% [E9, E10]. Moreover, institutional money flow remains distinctly positive with a holding change of +1.16 percentage points, anchored by domestic institutions increasing their stake to 2.23% [E39, E40]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the company a high confidence score of 96 out of 100 on the back of strong continuing sales and net profit expansion [E58, E59, E61].

Conceded: the company demonstrates 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth of 45% and 36% respectively, alongside a TTM profit growth of 36% [E17, E18, E19]. Conceded: ROCE stands at 14.89% against a sector benchmark of 6.91%, and ROE sits at 19.33% versus the sector's 5.35% [E9, E10]. Conceded: domestic institutions and foreign institutions have increased their holdings, contributing to positive institutional money flow [E38, E39, E40]. However, this reported profit growth is entirely disconnected from cash generation, evidenced by an extreme negative operating cash flow of Rs -272 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -275 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31, E32]. This severe cash burn has forced borrowings to surge more than fourfold from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in a single year [E35]. Furthermore, high short-term operational risks are underscored by ballooning debtor days that have deteriorated from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E57]. Finally, despite the high screen score, recent price performance already outpaces profit growth by 24%, meaning market expectations are running well ahead of operational reality [E53, E58].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow were deeply negative at Rs -272 Cr and Rs -275 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32], borrowings rose to Rs 324 Cr [E35], and debtor days expanded to 76.3 days [E57]. However, the bear ignores that these cash and working capital pressures are embedded in a business with a rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 [E58], backed by robust multi-year fundamental outperformance where 5-year profit growth of 45% outpaces long-term share price appreciation of 28% [E52]. Conceded: recent price growth has outpaced profit growth by 24% [E53], but the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price of ₹ 1,033 only implies an achievable 8.8% earnings growth rate compared to the 18.0% base case [E43]. Furthermore, institutional participation remains robust and positive with combined domestic and foreign holdings expanding across the board [E38, E39, E40], validating the underlying franchise value. Operating margins continue to expand structurally, rising by 1 percentage point in the TTM and 2 percentage points in the June 2026 quarter [E26, E27], proving that operational efficiency remains firmly intact despite the short-term working capital stretch.

Conceded: the rules-based screen score is 96 out of 100 [E58], and 5-year profit growth has outpaced share price growth [E52]. However, the bull's reliance on backward-looking growth metrics completely sidesteps the alarming liquidity crisis revealed in March 2026, where operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs -272 Cr [E31], free cash flow plunged to negative Rs -275 Cr [E32], and cash conversion worsened to a severe -3.89x [E30]. This cash burn has directly fueled a massive surge in borrowings from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in a single year [E35], while debtor days simultaneously bloated from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E57]. Conceded: the reverse DCF implies a modest 8.8% growth rate [E43], but that theoretical cushion is meaningless when actual short-term debt nearly quadruples and working capital fails to convert into real cash. Finally, pointing to institutional buying [E38, E39, E40] or a 1 percentage point TTM margin expansion [E26] cannot mask the fundamental risk of an annualized volatility rating of 52.8% [E50] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% [E49] in a cyclical earnings profile [E54].
